# Australia’s Infrastructure Challenge is One of Distance


### Australia is facing a unique infrastructure challenge: **distance.**


Additionally, Australia must manage population growth, urbanization and aging infrastructure as it increases demand for the systems that support modern life, from transportation and water networks to hospitals, ports, railways and data centers.


Across a continent of huge scale, building infrastructure isn’t simply about having the right materials or expertise. It’s about getting them to the right place, reliably and at the scale and specification required. This is where CRH has a distinctive role to play.


In Australia, building the infrastructure of the future means overcoming the challenge of distance. Through our connected businesses across Australia, we combine local expertise with the scale, locations and logistics capabilities to support infrastructure *wherever* it’s needed.

## Connected by design, positioned for growth


As demand for critical infrastructure across transportation, reindustrialization and water continues to grow, CRH’s connected businesses and nationwide footprint are well positioned to support customers no matter where they are in the country of Australia.


Our strategically-located asset network and integrated logistics capabilities provides a strong competitive advantage.


## Port Melbourne Cement Terminal


The Port Melbourne Cement Terminal is one of Australia’s most strategically important cement supply hubs, serving Victoria’s construction market from a prime location within the Port of Melbourne. Approximately 75% of the state’s cement demand passes through this facility! The terminal can receive product from self-unloading vessels at rates of up to 1,320 tons per hour and simultaneously load four truck lanes for onward distribution to customers across Victoria.


## Yarraville Grinding Station


Located on Melbourne’s inner western waterfront, the Yarraville Grinding Station is a key component of CRH’s cementitious materials strategy in Australia. The site was the country’s first facility dedicated to grinding granulated blast furnace slag, positioning it at the forefront of supplementary cementitious materials development. Through its integrated network, the site processes imported materials and connected them to downstream concrete, packaged products, building materials and infrastructure solutions.
